facts.label: Hottest point
facts.value: About 2,000 K, just east of noon

controls.label: NIRSpec
controls.qualification: Published map · Challener et al. 2024 · JWST NIRSpec 2023 phase curve
controls.notes: Brightness temperature fitted to JWST light curves; large patterns only. The hot spot sits about 7° east of noon and south of the equator; how far south depends on the model, 4° to 16°.

controls.label: NIRSpec refit
controls.qualification: Our fit of the same light curve · spin axis on the orbit normal
controls.notes: The published light curve refitted here with the same model, the planet spinning about its orbit's axis. Converted with a model spectrum of the star, not a blackbody.

controls.label: MIRI
controls.qualification: Our map from raw JWST exposures · 5–10.5 µm · 2022 phase curve
controls.notes: Reduced here from the raw MIRI exposures and fitted here. Dayside and nightside averages agree with Bell et al. (2024).

controls.label: MIRI 5–6.5 µm
controls.notes: The same reduction, light from 5 to 6.5 µm only. Only large patterns are real.

controls.label: MIRI 6.5–8.5 µm
controls.notes: The same reduction, light from 6.5 to 8.5 µm only. Only large patterns are real.

controls.label: MIRI 8.5–10.5 µm
controls.qualification: Our map · longest usable MIRI slice
controls.notes: The same reduction, light from 8.5 to 10.5 µm only. Beyond 10.5 µm the fit breaks down. Only large patterns are real.
